title: How to Read a Weather Forecast

cover.alt: Mature woman checks a mixed-weather forecast before leaving home with a jacket, bag, and umbrella ready.

blocks.title: Weather Forecasts
paragraphs: Reading a weather forecast to plan your day is a useful daily skill. A forecast can show temperature, clouds, wind, and rain chance. You can use those four clues to choose clothes, decide what to bring, and make a backup plan.

items.prompt: Where do you usually check the weather — on your phone, on TV, or somewhere else?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: I check the weather on my phone every morning.

items.prompt: What weather words do you already know in English?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: sunny, rain, cold, hot, wind.

items.prompt: Can you think of a time when the weather changed your plans?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: It rained and I could not go to the park.

blocks.title: Temperature: Hot, Warm, Cool, or Cold
paragraphs: A forecast often shows a high temperature and a low temperature. The high is the warmest temperature expected. The low is the coolest. First check whether the numbers use Celsius or Fahrenheit. Imagine a high of 22°C and a low of 12°C. A light shirt may work at midday, but you may want a jacket later.

images.alt: A daily high of 22 degrees Celsius with a light shirt and a low of 12 degrees Celsius with a light jacket.

items.prompt: The high is 22°C and the low is 12°C. Why might you bring a jacket?
items.answer: The day may feel warm at midday, but it can be much cooler later.

blocks.title: Sky Conditions: Sunny, Partly Cloudy, and Cloudy
paragraphs: Sky words describe how much of the sky has clouds. The National Weather Service uses sunny or clear for very few clouds. Partly cloudy means some clouds and some open sky. Cloudy means clouds cover nearly all the sky. Clouds alone do not tell you the rain chance, so check the rain percent too.

images.alt: Three views compare sunny, partly cloudy, and cloudy skies.

items.prompt: If a forecast says partly cloudy, what will the sky look like?
items.answer: There will be some clouds and some open sky.

blocks.title: Wind: Light, Breezy, and Windy
paragraphs: A wind forecast gives a direction and a speed. The speed may be in miles per hour, or mph. The National Weather Service calls 0–5 mph light wind, 15–25 mph breezy, and 20–30 mph windy. The ranges can overlap, so read the number too. On a breezy day, hold loose things and choose a jacket that closes.

items.prompt: A forecast says breezy at 18 mph. Which information is most exact: the word or the number?
items.answer: The number, 18 mph, is the most exact information.

blocks.title: Rain Chance: What Percent Means
paragraphs: A rain percent is the probability of precipitation, or POP. It is the chance of measurable rain at your location during the forecast period. It is not the percent of the day that it will rain. The National Weather Service calls 20% a slight chance, 30–50% a chance, and 60–70% likely. Always check which time period the percent describes.

images.alt: Forecast cards compare a 20 percent slight chance, 40 percent chance, and 70 percent likely rain for one place and time.

items.prompt: What does a 60% rain chance for the afternoon mean?
items.answer: Rain is likely at your location during the afternoon forecast period.

blocks.title: Reading a Full Forecast
paragraphs: Now imagine this forecast: high 22°C, low 12°C, partly cloudy, breezy at 18 mph, and 60% rain in the afternoon. Bring a light jacket for the cooler time. Keep a hat secure in the wind. Take an umbrella and choose an indoor backup for the afternoon. One short forecast can help you make several useful choices.

items.prompt: For this forecast, what three useful things could you bring?
items.answer: You could bring a light jacket, an umbrella, and a bag that keeps loose things secure.

items.prompt: Look at tomorrow's forecast. What will you wear, what will you bring, and what backup plan could help?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: 'It will be cool and rain is likely. I will wear a jacket, bring an umbrella, and choose an indoor place if it rains.'

a noticeable wind; NWS uses this for 15–25 mph
the chance of measurable rain or snow at a place during a time period
